correctness.rationale: Enumerating the four IID versus two reshuffling row products gives D=¼(B⁴+C⁴−BC²B−CB²C). For rank-one projections P,Q and β=α(2−α), multiplication gives D=β[(β+α²ρ²)(P+Q)−2α(PQ+QP)]/4. The eigenvectors u±v and exact eigenvalues are established algebraically, including equality and sharp sign reversal. One-step conditional contraction for IID and deterministic two-sweep strict contraction for RR prove separate long-run convergence. A standalone exact-rational verifier checks 202 matrix/eigen/witness cases but is not used to infer all-real quantifiers.

limitations: Exactly two normalized, consistent real equations, common 0<α<2, two updates, Euclidean solution-error comparison; no many-row, noise, rounding, or universal multiepoch ranking.

value.rationale: The natural algorithm-design question of replacing independent row sampling by an epoch permutation has a surprising exact boundary under overrelaxation. The sharp formula quantifies dependence on row coherence and initial-error orientation; an explicit rational example shows reshuffling is worse despite both algorithms converging. This is not a routine coordinate renaming or a marginal numerical improvement, and avoids unsupported claims about many rows or later epochs.
